source.title: When does Privileged Information Explain Away Label Noise?
source.authors: Guillermo Ortiz-Jiménez; Mark Collier; Anant Nawalgaria; A. D'Amour; Jesse Berent; Rodolphe Jenatton; Effrosyni Kokiopoulou

record.tranche_reason: The study measures training dynamics on clean and mislabeled examples in noisy-label datasets, using PI methods and a no-PI baseline. It does not reproduce the random-label experiments in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports training-dynamics results for clean and mislabeled examples, which bear on V6. Its citations to random-label memorization are prior work, not study results. The accuracy curves are figure-only; the prose describes their patterns.
record.test_reason: The study plots its own standard no-PI baseline's training accuracy separately on clean and mislabeled examples, bearing on V6. The extracted rows instead describe PI interventions designed to accelerate memorization or suppress it in another head; those results alone do not establish the natural clean-before-noise ordering.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: helpful PI separates clean from mislabeled examples and enables an easier memorization shortcut for mislabeled examples, protecting feature learning. Overly predictive PI can also impede clean-feature learning, and suitable PI methods can complement other noise-handling techniques.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates privileged information methods on real and synthetic noisy-label datasets; it does not apply the original random-label intervention or measure the original claim's training and test errors.
record.method_sensitivity: PI feature type changes the training dynamics; the results also vary by dataset and by PI versus no-PI head.

fits_no_version.finding: Providing labels as PI rapidly yields 100% PI-head training accuracy; selectively providing noisy targets accelerates their PI-head memorization while protecting clean-feature learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Privileged information can deliberately redirect noisy-label memorization into a shortcut, changing learning dynamics across heads.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202, 2023
record.problems: The dynamics relevant to V6 are principally shown in figures, without numerical curve values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use noisy labels and PI methods rather than completely random labels under standard training.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified curve values could be extracted from Figures 2 and 6–10; the retained rows capture the text-described CIFAR-10H dynamics relevant to V6. Other training-dynamics plots are not separately rowed because the paper gives no precise numeric values or distinct textual outcome for them.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error and chance test performance under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time for true and random labels, including convergence across corruption fractions.
Perfect fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption sweep from none to all with perfect training fit and steadily deteriorating test performance.
Necessity and sufficiency of weight decay, dropout and augmentation for random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Completely random-label datasets and the original Arpit experimental setup; the available baseline dynamics concern mixed clean and noisy labels.

missing.what: Extract the standard no-PI baseline's clean and mislabeled training-accuracy trajectories together, including their relative learning order. These controls bear directly on V6 but are absent from the rows. The supplied text preserves axes and legends without readable curves, so their outcome cannot be determined. The record's omission statement does not specifically identify this essential control comparison.
missing.locator: Figure 2, central column; Appendix E.1, Figures 6–10

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is assigned from the engineered PI rows. The related-work statement that incorrect labels are memorized later cites prior research. Appendix D.1 reports worse test performance without early stopping, but that alone does not establish the clean-versus-noisy learning order required by V6.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random training labels to zero or near-zero error with test error at chance, without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels compared with true labels, and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A controlled sweep from no corruption to fully random labels, perfect training fit throughout, and steadily increasing test error.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
The study compares clean and mislabeled examples during training, but does not compare real labels with completely random labels or test the cited Arpit et al. setup.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training accuracy on clean and mislabeled examples over training for TRAM with annotator labels as PI.
rows.value: Figure only; text says the label model quickly obtains 100% training accuracy on all examples using the PI head.
rows.note: The prose reports the 100% pattern; the figure is the only source for the curve over epochs.
rows.check: Labels supplied directly as PI deliberately enable fitting all examples quickly. The stated 100% accuracy is correct, but does not measure learning real patterns before noise. Specify CIFAR-10H worst.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training accuracy on clean and mislabeled examples over training for TRAM with annotator labels as PI.
rows.value: Figure only; text says fitting all examples with the PI head slows training of the no-PI head.
rows.note: The figure shows the training curve; prose explicitly describes the slowdown.
rows.check: The prose describes slowed no-PI-head training generally, not a measured clean-versus-mislabeled learning order. This head uses representations trained through the PI head and is not the standard no-PI baseline. Specify CIFAR-10H worst.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training accuracy on clean and mislabeled examples over training for TRAM with near-optimal PI.
rows.value: Figure only; text says near-optimal models train fastest on the mislabeled examples on the PI head.
rows.note: The text describes the relative training rate; the plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: Near-optimal PI supplies the noisy target specifically on mislabeled examples, deliberately accelerating their memorization. Fastest compares PI configurations, not noisy-label learning against clean-label learning. Specify CIFAR-10H worst.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training accuracy on clean and mislabeled examples over training for TRAM with near-optimal PI.
rows.value: Figure only; text says training is very slow on mislabeled examples on the no-PI head.
rows.note: This is the text's qualitative description of the plotted training curve.
rows.check: Slow noisy-label learning is produced by an engineered PI shortcut and gradient routing. Alone it cannot establish V6's natural learning order; partial is not justified. Specify CIFAR-10H worst.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training accuracy on clean and mislabeled examples over training for TRAM with near-optimal PI.
rows.value: Figure only; text says performance on the correct examples is much higher.
rows.note: The prose describes the clean-example result qualitatively; no numerical accuracy is stated.
rows.check: Higher clean-example accuracy under near-optimal PI describes the intervention's benefit, not evidence that clean examples are learned before noisy ones under ordinary training. The quoted comparison does not provide a temporal ordering. Specify CIFAR-10H worst.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10H TRAM training dynamics with annotator-label and near-optimal PI
reader_labels.reason: The study reports different training dynamics for clean and mislabeled examples: PI can fit mislabeled examples quickly while the no-PI head learns them more slowly and performance on correct examples is higher (R1–R5). This supports a clean/noisy learning distinction in this setting, but does not test completely random labels.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The measured dynamics depend on PI type and head; the study does not establish that ordinary networks learn real versus completely random labels differently (R1–R5).
